description: Answers 'do you come to my town?' in a few seconds: lists of towns served, coverage maps, branch or yard locations with hours, and per-town links that double as local SEO pages. It should end with a fallback for people outside the list.
queries: areas we serve section with list of cities
delivery coverage area map section with zip code check

references.layout: Two-column split. Left ~40%: 4-line bold heading, then a small 2-line note with an underlined link near the bottom. Right ~60%: three columns of ~9 city names each with ~8px line gaps; the last column ends with an underlined 'View All'. Under the list: 'Don't see your city?' followed by an outlined pill button 'Join the waitlist'.
references.type: Rounded grotesk (Cereal-like). Heading ~30px semibold, line-height ~1.1, black. City names ~13px regular grey. Button ~10px medium.
references.color: White page; heading ~#222; list ~#717171; button white fill with 1px ~#222 border.
details: Qualifiers like 'Metro' and 'County' set expectations about reach
Plain text names, not chips or badges
Explicit fallback for anyone not on the list
List columns are left-aligned and sit on the heading's top line
references.why_it_works: Quiet, scannable and honest, and the 'don't see your city?' line catches edge cases instead of losing them.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Proudly serving Union County' on the left; towns on the right (Westfield, Cranford, Scotch Plains, Garwood...). Fallback: 'Don't see your town? Call (908) 555-0142, we often go 30 miles out.'

references.layout: Small-caps eyebrow 'GLOBAL IMPACT', heavy condensed headline (~32px). A large light-grey rounded panel holds a left column of 3 big stats (number + label, each with a thin vertical rule on its left) and a white dotted map on the right. Small square red markers connect by thin vertical leader lines to labels like 'Utah / Since 2022' and 'Bay Area (HQ) / Since 2014'. A 4-up stat row sits under the panel.
references.type: Condensed grotesk bold for headline and stat numbers (~28-32px). Place labels ~8px red; 'Since YYYY' ~8px grey. Stat labels ~9px.
references.color: Off-white page ~#f3f2ee; panel ~#e8e6e1; map land white; markers and place names red ~#e8452c; text ~#111.
details: Leader lines with 'Since YEAR' show how long they have served each place
Stats and map share one panel, so numbers read as facts about the map
Square markers instead of teardrop pins
Map is drawn flat in white on grey, not an embedded tile map
references.why_it_works: Where, how long and how much in one glance. The 'since' detail builds trust in a way a bare pin never does.
references.trade_adaptation: Roofer or HVAC: county outline with leader-line labels 'Westfield, since 2009', 'Summit, since 2014'; stats '2,140 roofs', '4.9★ from 312 reviews', '18 towns'.

references.layout: Centered stack of 4 city names, one per line, very large (~64px). The active city ('LONDON') is italic and near-black, with small pink name tags (first names of staff) pinned onto its letters; the other cities are upright and light grey. Under the stack, a small off-white card (~230x40) with address, phone and an underlined email for the active city. Tiny 'LOCATIONS' eyebrow top-left.
references.type: Condensed high-contrast serif (Editorial New / Canela-like), uppercase, ~64px; active line italic. Card text sans ~9px. Name tags ~6px bold uppercase.
references.color: Warm greige ~#e6e1db; active ~#2a1d1d; inactive ~#bdb3ab; tags pink ~#f29ac0; info card ~#f6f3ef.
details: Active/inactive state is italic + dark vs upright + grey
People's first names pinned to the active city
Contact card only shows the selected city's details
Type is the map: no map graphic at all
references.why_it_works: Turns a list of places into a brand statement while staying usable: pick a town, get its details.
references.trade_adaptation: Painter or landscaper with 5-8 towns: stack the names; selecting one shows 'Crew lead: Marco, usually there within 2 hrs, (908) 555-0142'. Name tags = crew leads.

references.layout: Black full-bleed. Centered, ragged stack of 7 city names in heavy condensed uppercase (~44px, leading ~0.95), each followed by a superscript data label ('21.1K', '10K', '13.1'). Bottom-right a large wordmark lockup; bottom-left a tiny red link list.
references.type: Heavy condensed grotesk (Futura Condensed / Druk-like), uppercase, ~44px; superscripts ~12px bold.
details: Superscript data attached to each name
One color, one typeface, no icons
Centered ragged edge makes the list into a shape
Tight leading so lines nearly touch
references.why_it_works: Maximum confidence with minimum parts; the superscripts add real information.
references.trade_adaptation: Bold industrial style for a roofer or electrician: 'WESTFIELD ¹² ᴹᴵᴺ', 'CRANFORD ¹⁸ ᴹᴵᴺ' (drive time) or 'SUMMIT ²¹⁴ ᴶᴼᴮˢ' (jobs done), in one brand color on black or concrete grey.

references.layout: Split section on a saturated field. Left ~50%: flat, cropped state map with served regions filled yellow and not-yet-served regions a darker orange, decorated with simple cloud and mountain illustrations. Right: small yellow tag 'SERVICE AREAS', a 6-line bold paragraph explaining current coverage and growth, then a 2-item legend with color squares.
references.type: Grotesk bold ~22px white for the paragraph; tag uppercase ~8px; legend ~10px regular.
references.color: Orange-red field ~#ff4a12; served ~#ffc93c; not-yet-served ~#ff7a22; white text; blue/indigo illustration accents ~#3b4bff.
details: Legend admits 'Areas not serviced yet'
Coverage explained in a sentence, not a list
Flat drawn map in brand colors instead of a Google embed
Section tag reused as a consistent label style across the site
references.why_it_works: Answers 'do you serve me?' visually in one look, and it is ownable because the map is in brand colors.
references.trade_adaptation: Pest control or landscaper: flat county outline with served townships filled in the brand color; legend 'Weekly routes' / 'Call for availability'; paragraph 'We cover all of Union County and the western edge of Essex.'

references.layout: Wide split card. Left ~30% text column bounded by a vertical rule: location name, address line, two lines of hours, a 6-line paragraph about the place, then two small outlined buttons 'GO TO MAP' / 'DOWNLOAD MENU'. Right ~70%: photo carousel (~8px radius) with a '01 — 03' counter and two square prev/next buttons at bottom-right.
references.type: Soft serif (Cooper / Recoleta-like) ~24px for the name; address ~10px in the accent color; hours and buttons in mono ~8px uppercase; paragraph sans ~8px.
references.color: Cream ~#fdf7ef; burnt orange ~#c75b12 for address, button borders and rules; text dark brown ~#3a2a20.
details: Hours set in mono so they read like a shop sign
Paragraph gives history and practical details (opened 2011, free street parking)
Small outlined uppercase buttons instead of big filled CTAs
Photo counter '01 — 03'
references.why_it_works: Makes a location feel like a real place with a history rather than an address.
references.trade_adaptation: Trade with a shop, yard or showroom (garage doors, remodeler, landscape supply): 'Our Westfield yard, since 1998', hours in mono, buttons 'Get directions' / 'See the showroom', carousel of the shop, trucks and crew.

references.layout: Left column (~170px): search input 'Enter a postcode or address' with magnifier, then a scrolling list of locations, each with a pin icon, bold name, address, underlined phone and email, and full Monday-Sunday hours. Right ~75%: grayscale map with black circular cluster markers showing counts (1, 5, 24, 2, 1) and zoom controls.
references.type: Sans ~9px; location names bold, hours regular; marker numbers ~10px bold white.
references.color: White list panel; desaturated map ~#e9e9e9 / ~#cfcfcf; markers ~#222 with white numerals.
details: Map is fully desaturated so the brand markers are the only contrast
Postcode search at the top of the list
Hours listed for every day, including 'Sunday Closed'
Cluster counts instead of dozens of overlapping pins
references.why_it_works: A functional locator done with restraint; the monochrome map matches a minimal brand instead of fighting it.
references.trade_adaptation: Zip checker for an HVAC or plumbing company: 'Enter your ZIP' returns 'Yes, we're in Westfield every weekday' plus the nearest crew base; grayscale map with branded van-base markers.

references.layout: Full-bleed orange-red field. A centered outlined oval label 'Our Stores' (~150x50, 1px white). Below, three centered address blocks of five lines each (neighborhood, street, city/state/ZIP, phone, hours) with ~24px between blocks. Three stacked white pill buttons at the bottom (email, Instagram, TikTok).
references.type: Grotesk ~16px regular white, line-height ~1.25, all lines the same size; pill labels ~9px.
references.color: Orange-red ~#f4511e field; white text; white pills with orange text.
details: Hand-drawn-looking oval outline as the section label
No hierarchy games: every line the same size, all info visible
Hours and phone in every block
Centered poster layout
references.why_it_works: Warm and poster-like, and everything a visitor needs is visible with zero clicks.
references.trade_adaptation: Trade with 1-3 bases or route zones: oval label 'Where we work', blocks like 'North County / Westfield, Cranford, Garwood / Mon-Wed / (908) 555-0142'.

references.layout: White card centered on a grey page. Heading 'Explore by region' (~18px bold), then a tab row (active tab with ~3px purple underline). Below, a 4-column grid of ~37 entries, each two lines: bold 'City, ST' and a lighter country line with a small flag.
references.type: Sans; city ~10px bold; country ~9px regular; tabs uppercase ~8px tracked.
references.color: White card; underline aubergine ~#4a154b; text ~#1d1c1d; secondary ~#616061.
details: Tabs chunk a long list into regions
'City, ST' bold format is easy to scan
Second line adds context under every town
Grid columns stay aligned regardless of name length
references.why_it_works: Handles a long coverage list without a wall of text.
references.trade_adaptation: Multi-county HVAC or pest company: tabs 'Union / Essex / Morris'; entries 'Westfield, NJ' bold with a second line 'Mon & Thu routes' or 'Same-day available'.

references.layout: Heading 'Browse by City' (~18px bold). A horizontal row of country filters (active = black pill, others plain text). Below, 5 columns, one per city: bold city header then 8 links in the form '[Service] in [City]'. A round arrow button at the right scrolls to more cities.
references.type: Sans; headers ~10px semibold; links ~8px regular, near-black.
references.color: White page; active pill ~#0d0d0d with white text; links ~#222.
details: Programmatic '[service] in [town]' link matrix: each link is a landing page
Pill filter for the top-level region
Horizontal scroll for more columns instead of a taller section
No decoration at all; pure navigation
references.why_it_works: Maps directly onto the local-SEO page structure trades need, without looking like spam.
references.trade_adaptation: Above the footer: one column per town, links 'Roof repair in Westfield', 'Gutter cleaning in Westfield', 'Skylight install in Westfield'; county pills on top.

references.layout: Left-aligned heading with the total ('460 IKEA stores in 62 markets'), a small 'Updated: 22 December 2022' line, then a large flat grey map with ~50px yellow circles per region, each holding the region name and a count.
references.type: Bold sans; heading ~22px; bubble labels ~8px bold, counts ~16px bold; date ~9px regular.
references.color: White page; map ~#cccccc; bubbles IKEA yellow ~#ffd426 with ~#111 text.
details: 'Updated' date stamp adds honesty
Numbers on the map instead of pins
Total stated in the heading so the map is supporting detail
Brand color only on the data
references.why_it_works: Coverage becomes a count you can read in two seconds.
references.trade_adaptation: County outline with brand-color bubbles 'Westfield 214', 'Cranford 167', 'Summit 98' (jobs completed); heading '1,900 jobs in 14 towns'; 'Updated Oct 2026'.

references.layout: Beige band; centered heading (~20px bold) with a one-line subline. A 4-column grid of flat white cards (~150x145, square corners, no shadow), each with a bold city name, a 3-4 line address, and a bottom-pinned 'GET DIRECTIONS' small-caps link with a right-aligned arrow.
references.type: Sans; city ~13px bold; address ~9px regular; CTA uppercase ~8px tracked.
references.color: Beige ~#f4ede4 band; white cards; text ~#1d1c1d; link blue ~#1264a3.
details: CTA pinned to the card bottom so rows align regardless of address length
Flat white cards on a warm band, no borders or shadows
Arrow right-aligned on the CTA row
Wrapping second row left-aligned, not centered
references.why_it_works: Clean, repeatable and practical; works for 2 cards or 12.
references.trade_adaptation: One card per county or crew: 'Union County' + towns covered + 'Call this crew →' pinned at the bottom.

takeaways: Open with a plain sentence of coverage ('We serve Union County and 18 surrounding towns') before any list or map.
A plain 3-4 column town list in ~13px grey beats chips, badges or pins, and it should end with a fallback: 'Don't see your town? Call us.'
Pick one strong visual device per site: a giant typographic town stack, a flat brand-colored county map, or an annotated map. Not all three.
Attach useful data to towns: drive time, years served ('since 2009'), jobs completed, route days. Superscripts and leader lines are the crafted way to do it.
If a real map is used, desaturate it to grayscale so brand markers carry it; flat drawn maps in brand colors are more ownable than embeds.
Set hours in mono or small caps so they read like a sign, and keep the phone number visible without a click.
Use the section for local SEO: '[service] in [town]' links double as navigation.
avoid: Unstyled full-color Google Maps iframes and repeated identical map tiles per office (SIGMA, Upwork): they read as template.
World maps and 'offices around the globe' framing (Customer.io, Klarna, Wise): wrong scale for a local trade.
Emoji or clip-art landmark icons per city (Cake's 🌴🎡🏰, Intercom line icons, HubSpot postage stamps): cute but generic.
Stock skyline photos per city (OpenTable, Wise): trades should show their own trucks, crews and jobs.
Purple-filled country choropleths: a SaaS cliché.
Unbounded alphabetical dumps of 200+ neighborhoods with no grouping (ClassPass).
Accordion-only lists where the town names are hidden behind clicks.
